Definition: from G3709; to provoke or enrage, i.e. (passively) become exasperated:--be angry (wroth).
BiblicalUsage: To be angry is a verb the Bible handles carefully. Jesus warned that whoever is angry with his brother without a cause is in danger of judgment, and Paul commands believers to be angry and sin not, and not to let the sun go down upon their wrath.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe anger is not always sin, but it is always dangerous: even righteous anger must not be given the night to settle into bitterness.
